title: upgrade attention kernels: flashattentionv2 + fused rotary/rope ops + scheduling tweaks
author: Evan Miller
description: Context: production workloads are seeing increased tail latency and overall cost for long-context chat workloads. This PR upgrades our attention kernels to FlashAttention v2 variants, fuses rotary/rope application into the attention kernel where possible, and adds scheduler heuristics to improve continuous batching and KV-cache friendly placement. Summary of changes: 1) vendor/flashattention: integrate FA v2 sources and build logic; expose two kernel paths (fa_v2_fast and fa_v2_stable) selectable at runtime. 2) runtime/kernel/attn_fused_ops.cu: fused rotary/rope application with query/key projection to eliminate an extra kernel launch for rotary embeddings. 3) runtime/scheduler/batching_policy.cpp: add sequence-length-aware continuous batcher and cost-model hints for kernel selection; includes soft-fallback to fa_v2_stable for edge cases. 4) runtime/kv/kv_cache_manager.cpp: ensure KV-cache alignment and prefetch hints for FA v2 tiled kernels. 5) tests/perf/attn_long_context.py: new microbenchmarks (latency, throughput, memory) and integration test to validate outputs match baseline within numerical tolerances. Motivation: FA v2 improves memory efficiency and throughput for long sequences; fusing rotary/rope reduces memory traffic and per-token latency; scheduler changes allow higher effective batching without violating latency SLOs. Backwards compatibility: behavior is opt-in via runtime config (ATTN_KERNEL_PREFERENCE) and falls back to previous implementation when models or hardware do not meet FA v2 constraints. Related: ENG-4621 (attention perf project), ENG-4729 (continuous batching roadmap). Checklist: - [x] Integrate FA v2 sources and CI compile - [x] Add fused-op kernel and unit tests - [x] Implement scheduler heuristics and e2e bench - [x] Update perf benchmarks and docs - [x] Run extended CI on p4d and a100 clusters - [x] Security review for vendor code (third-party license checked)

release_notes: Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttention v2 with fused rotary/rope ops, scheduler improvements for continuous batching, KV-cache alignment fixes. Expected impact: ~1.2-1.4x throughput for long-context workloads and reduced per-token latency; opt-in via ATTENTION_KERNEL_PREFERENCE.
notes_for_operators: Runtime flag ATTENTION_KERNEL_PREFERENCE accepts: auto | fa_v2_fast | fa_v2_stable | legacy. Default 'auto' selects kernel based on model length distribution and hardware capabilities. If experiencing numerical drift on fp16, set to 'legacy' for parity. New vendor tree increases binary size by ~3MB; ensure artifact cache policies account for this.
benchmark_summary: On p4d (fp16, 8k context), fa_v2_fast + fused-rotary: throughput +25% vs legacy; p99 latency -14%. On a100 tiled kernels: throughput +18%, memory peak -12%. Numeric regression: max absolute diff < 1e-3 on fp16 outputs for test set of 2000 tokens.
